research_rationale:
EO 13666 (79 FR 22591, signed 2014-04-18; held official Federal Register text) is a one-sentence amending order. After the authority recital it states that Executive Order 12019 of November 3, 1977 (Establishing the Defense Meritorious Service Medal) is amended by inserting a phrase extending award of the medal to members of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation after the words 'any member of the Armed Forces of the United States' in section 1 of EO 12019. The dossier inventory covered only the authority recital (characters 719-861) and omitted the amending sentence, so one inventory override covers the recital and the amending sentence (characters 719-1122 of the held text), and nothing in the order lies outside it. The order has no sunset, condition or effective-date clause, and the held text of EO 12019 (read in full) has none either. The amending command was performed when the order issued; what remains is the amended section 1 of EO 12019. The held U.S. Code note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints EO 12019 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13666, Apr. 18, 2014, 79 F.R. 22591' with section 1 reading 'to any member of the Armed Forces of the United States, or to any member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation', and gives no ending statement. The packet holds no later order amending, revoking or superseding either EO 13666 or EO 12019 (later-events chain empty; the OFR catalog search records no disposition; a search of the held texts for 'Executive Order 12019' finds only EO 12019 itself, its 1989 codification entry, EO 13666 and copies of EO 13666). The U.S. Code release point is current through 2026-10-09, so the note itself does not cover 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14; the OFR catalog search records no disposition of EO 13666 or EO 12019.

Executive Order 12916 of May 13, 1994
Implementation of the Border Environment Cooperation  
Commission and the North American Development Bank
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the North American Free 
Trade Agreement Implementation Act, Public Law 103-182; 107 Stat. 2057 
(“NAFTA Implementation A ct”), and section 301 of title 3, United States 
Code, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. The Agreement Between the Government of the United States 
of America and the Government of the United M exican States Concerning 
the Establishment of a Border Environment Cooperation Commission and 
a North American Development Bank (“Agreement”) shall be implemented 
consistent with United States policy for the protection of human, animal 
or plant life or health, and the environment. The Agreement shall also 
be implemented to advance sustainable development, pollution prevention, 
environmental justice, ecosystem protection, and biodiversity preservation 
and in a manner that promotes transparency and public participation in 
accordance with the North American Free Trade Agreement and the Agree­
ment.
Sec. 2. (a) The Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency and 
the United States Commissioner, International Boundary and Water Commis­
sion, United States and M exico (“Commissioner”), shall represent the United 
States as Members of the Board of Directors of the Border Environment 
Cooperation Commission in accordance with the Agreement.
(b) The policies and positions of the United States in the Border Environ­
ment Cooperation Commission shall be coordinated through applicable inter­
agency procedures, which shall include participation by the Department 
of State, the Department of the Treasury, the Department of Housing and 
Urban Development, the Department of the Interior, the Agency for Inter­
national Development, the Environmental Protection Agency, and, as appro­
priate, other Federal agencies.
(c) The Commissioner shall promote cooperation, as appropriate, between 
the International Boundary and Water Commission and the Border Environ­
ment Cooperation Commission in planning, developing, carrying out border 
sanitation, and other environmental activities.
Sec. 3. (a) The United States Government representatives to the Board of 
the North American Development Bank shall be the Secretary of the Treasury, 
the Secretary of State, and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection 
Agency.
(b) For purposes of loans or guarantees for projects certified by the Border 
Environment Cooperation Commission, the representatives shall be instructed 
in accordance with the procedures of the National Advisory Council on 
International Monetary and Financial Policies (“C ouncil”) as established 
by Executive Order No. 11269. For purposes of this section only, the member­
ship of the Council shall be expanded to include the Secretary of the 
Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Secretary of the Interior, 
and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency.

ommendations of the Community Adjustment and Investment Program Fi­

Executive Order 11269
NATIONAL ADVISORY COUNCIL ON INTERNATIONAL MONETARY AND
FINANCIAL POLICIES
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Reorganization Plan No. 4 
of 1965 (30 F.R. 9353), and as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Establishment of Council,  (a) There is hereby estab­
lished the National Advisory Council on International Monetary and 
Financial Policies, hereinafter referred to as the Council.
(b) The Council shall be composed of the following members : the 
Secretary of the Treasury, who shall be the chairman of the Council, 
the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, the Chairman of 
the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and the Presi­
dent of the Export-Import Bank of Washington.
(c) Whenever matters within the jurisdiction of the Council may 
be of interest to Federal agencies not represented on the Council under 
Section 1  (b) of this prder, the Chairman of the Council may consult 
with such agencies and may invite them to designate representatives 
to participate in meetings and deliberations of the Council.
S ec. 2 . Functions of the Council,  (a) Exclusive of the functions 
delegated by the provisions of Section 3, below, and subject to the 
limitations contained in subsection (b) of this Section, all of the func­
tions which are now vested in the President in consequence of their 
transfer to him effected by the provisions of Section 1 (b) of Reorga­
nization Plan No. 4 of 1965 are hereby delegated to the Council. >
(b) The functions under Sections 4(a) and 4(b) (3) of the Bretton 
Woods Agreements Act, including those made applicable to the Inter­
national Finance Corporation, the Inter-American Development 
Bank, and the International Development Association (22 Ü.S.C. 
286b(a) and (b)(3);  282b; 283b; 284b), to the extent that such 
functions consist of coordination of policies, are hereby delegated to 
the Council. The functions so delegated shall be deemed to include 
the authority to review proposed individual loan, financial, exchange, 
or monetary transactions to the extent necessary or desirable to effec­
tuate the coordination of policies.
S ec. 3. Functions of the Secretary of the Treasury,  (a) Functions 
which are now vested in the President m consequence of their transfer 
to him effected by the provisions of Section 1 (b) ox Reorganization 
Plan No. 4 of 1965 are hereby delegated to the Secretary of the Treas­
ury to the extent of the following :
(1) Authority to instruct representatives of the United States to 
international financial organizations.
(2) Authority provided for in Section 4(b)(4)  of the Bretton 
Woods Agreements Act (22 U.S.C. 286b (b) (4) ).
(b) In carrying out the functions delegated to him by subsection
(a) of this Section the Secretary shall consult with the Council.
(c) Nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from the 
responsibilities of the Secretary of State with respect to the foreign 
policy of the United States.

ment, including representatives of the United States to international 
financial orgamzations, (1) shall keep the Council or the Secretary of 
the Treasury, as the case may be, fully informed concerning the 
foreign loan, financial, exchange, and monetary transactions in which 
they engage or may engage or with respect to which they have other

research_rationale:
EO 11269 (31 FR 2813, signed 1966-02-14, effective as of 1966-01-01; held official Federal Register text) establishes the National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies (section 1: establishment, membership of the Secretary of the Treasury as chairman and four named officers, and consultation with other agencies), delegates to the Council the functions transferred to the President by Reorganization Plan No. 4 of 1965 and certain Bretton Woods Agreements Act coordination functions (section 2), delegates to the Secretary of the Treasury the instruction of representatives to international financial organizations and the authority under section 4(b)(4) of that Act, subject to consultation with the Council (section 3), requires agencies to keep the Council and the Secretary informed (section 4), renames the Council in section 2(a) of Executive Order 10033 (section 5) and fixes the effective date (section 6). The dossier's 15 clauses are restated as 14 clauses cut from the held text: the dossier rows that split section 3(b) across a line break are merged, and every other row keeps its span. Sections 1 to 4 have no term or sunset. Sections 5 and 6 are spent: the renaming amendment of EO 10033 and the effective-date provision operated when the order was issued on 1966-02-14, with the order made effective retroactively as of 1966-01-01 by section 6. Later held orders amend sections 1(b), 2, 3 and 4 and add subsections 2(c), 3(d) and 3(e) and a section 7, and none ends a clause: EO 11334 (1967-03-07) adds 2(c) and 3(d) for the Asian Development Bank; EO 11808 (1974-09-30) adds the Assistant to the President for Economic Affairs to 1(b); EO 11977 (1977-03-14) adds the African Development Fund to 2(c) and 3(d) and adds 3(e); EO 12164 (signed 1979-09-29, effective as of 1979-10-01) adds the Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency to 1(b) and 4(a)(2), amends 3(a)(1), 3(a)(2) and 3(e) and adds section 7; EO 12188 (effective as of 1980-01-02) adds the United States Trade Representative to 1(b); EO 12403 (1983-02-08), EO 12567 (1986-10-02), EO 12647 (1988-08-02) and EO 12766 (1991-06-18) successively replace the list of institutions named in 2(c), 3(d) and 7; EO 12916 (1994-05-13) expands the Council's membership for the purposes of one section of that order only; and EO 13118 (effective as of 1999-04-01) replaces the Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development in 1(b) and with the Secretary of State in 4(a) and section 7. Orders that recite the Council without changing it (EO 12757 of 1991-03-19, EO 13345 of 2004-07-08) are not ends. The 2006-07-05 candidate in the dossier is a State Department delegation of authority that cites EO 12163 and does not mention EO 11269. The latest held order that treats the Council as existing is EO 13345 (2004-07-08), which refers to 'the National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies (Council) established by Executive Order 11269 of February 14, 1966'. Limits stated plainly: the U.S. Code and eCFR records in the packet are custody-record-only sources and are not cited; the packet holds no consolidated text of EO 11269 as amended, and the clause states rest on the original, the held amending orders and the absence of any revocation or supersession in the bounded searches.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause is subsection (b) of section 2 of EO 12458, which amended section 1-301(c) of EO 12163 to read '(except chapters 4, 6 and 8 thereof)'. EO 12560 section 8 (1986-05-24) restated section 1-301(c) to read in full, keeping those words. EO 13118 section 3 then struck 'part II of the Act (except chapters 4, 6, and 8 thereof)' from section 301(c) and inserted 'chapters 2 and 5 of part II of the Act', effective as of April 1, 1999, so the words EO 12458 inserted ended on 1999-04-01. The 1986 restatement is a later event, not the end, because it kept the words.

research_rationale:
EO 12458 (49 FR 1977, signed 1984-01-14; held official Federal Register text) amends Executive Order 12163 (Administration of Foreign Assistance and Related Functions) in three sections. Section 1 adds paragraphs (23), (24) and (25) at the end of section 1-201(a); section 2 amends section 1-301(a) and (c) by replacing '(except chapters 4 and 6 thereof)' with '(except chapters 4, 6 and 8 thereof)'; section 3 amends section 1-801(b) in the same way and section 1-801(c) by replacing 'chapter 6' with 'chapters 6 and 8'. The dossier inventory (headings and subsections) is restated as seven clauses cut from the held text: the three paragraphs of section 1, subsections (a) and (c) of section 2 and subsections (b) and (c) of section 3, with each section's lead-in included in its first clause. Each clause is an amending command performed on issuance; what matters for 2026-10-14 is whether the amended text of EO 12163 still contained the words it inserted. The amended targets were changed by later held orders. (1) EO 12560 (51 FR 19159, signed 1986-05-24; no separate effective-date clause) section 2 amends section 1-201(a) 'by deleting paragraphs (7), (22), (23), (25), (26), and (27), renumbering the remaining paragraphs accordingly'. EO 12458 had added (23) to (25) at the end of a list that ran to (22), so on that date (23) (section 512 of the 1982 appropriations act) and (25) (the El Salvador and Haiti functions under Public Law 98-151) were the paragraphs EO 12458 added, and they were deleted; that identification rests on the paragraph numbering stated in the held orders. Paragraph (24) (chapter 8 of part II of the Act) was not deleted by that order and was renumbered. (2) EO 13118 (64 FR 16595, signed 1999-03-31; 'shall become effective as of April 1, 1999') section 2 restates Part 1-2 of EO 12163 (which contains section 1-201) 'to read as follows' as the United States Agency for International Development part, with no paragraph on chapter 8 of part II; no held order between 1984 and 1999 names the section 573(d)(3) proviso of paragraph (24). Paragraph (24) therefore ended on 1999-04-01 when Part 1-2 was restated. (3) EO 12560 section 8 (1986-05-24) restates section 1-301(c) to read in full, keeping the words 'except chapters 4, 6, and 8 thereof'; EO 13118 section 3 then strikes 'part II of the Act (except chapters 4, 6, and 8 thereof)' from section 301(c) and inserts 'chapters 2 and 5 of part II of the Act', effective 1999-04-01, which ended section 2(c) of EO 12458. Title 3— The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11701
Employment of Veterans by Federal Agencies and Government 
Contractors and Subcontractors
On June 16, 1971, I issued Executive Order No. 11598 to facilitate 
the employment of returning veterans by requiring Federal agencies 
and Federal contractors and their subcontractors to list employment 
openings with the employment service systems. Section 503 of the Viet­
nam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act of 1972 (Public Law 
92-540; 86 Stat. 1097) added a new section 2012 to Title 38 of the 
United States Code which, in effect, provides statutory authority to 
extend the program developed under that order with respect to Govern­
ment contractors and their subcontractors.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Se c t io n 1. The Secretary of Labor shall issue rules and regulations 
requiring each department and agency of the executive branch of the 
Federal Government to list suitable employment openings with the 
appropriate office of the State Employment Service or the United 
States Employment Service. This section shall not be construed as 
requiring the employment of individuals referred by such office or as 
superseding any requirements of the Civil Service Laws. Rules, regula­
tions, and orders to implement this section shall be developed in 
consultation with the Civil Service Commission.
Sec. 2. The Secretary of Labor is hereby designated and empowered 
to exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the 
President, the authority of the President under Section 2012 of Title 38 
of the United States Code.
Sec. 3. The Secretary of Labor shall gather information on the 
effectiveness of the program established under this order and Section 
2012 of Title 38 of the United States Code and of the extent to which 
the employment service system is fulfilling the employment needs of 
veterans. The Secretary of Labor shall, from time to time, report to 
the President concerning his evaluation of the effectiveness of this order 
along with his recommendations for further action which the Secretary 
believes to be appropriate.
Sec. 4. Appropriate departments and agencies shall, in consultation 
with the Secretary of Labor, issue such amendments or additions to
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 38, N O . 18— M O N D AY, JANU ARY 29, 1973

procurement rules and regulations as may be necessary to carry out

ments and agencies are directed-to cooperate with the Secretary of 
Labor, to furnish the Secretary of Labor with such information and 
assistance as he may require in the performance of his functions under 
this order, and to comply with rules, regulations, and orders of the 
Secretary.
Sec. 5. Executive Order No. 11598 of June 16, 1971, is hereby

research_rationale:
EO 11701 (38 FR 2675, signed 1973-01-24; held official Federal Register text) has five sections: (1) the Secretary of Labor shall issue rules requiring each executive department and agency to list suitable employment openings with the State Employment Service or the United States Employment Service, in consultation with the Civil Service Commission; (2) the Secretary of Labor is designated and empowered to exercise, without presidential approval, the President's authority under section 2012 of title 38, United States Code (now 38 U.S.C. 4212); (3) the Secretary shall gather information on the program's effectiveness and report to the President from time to time; (4) agencies shall issue procurement rule amendments in consultation with the Secretary and cooperate with and comply with the Secretary's rules; (5) Executive Order No. 11598 of June 16, 1971 is superseded. The dossier inventory (sections 1 to 5, characters 1433-3614 of the held text) matches the sections of the held original. Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 outright and was performed when the order issued on 1973-01-24. Sections 1 to 4 have no sunset, condition or own-terms end. The held U.S. Code note to 38 U.S.C. 4212 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints EO 11701 in full ('Ex. Ord. No. 11701, Jan. 24, 1973, 38 F.R. 2675, provided:') with no ending statement and no amendment, and 25 U.S.C. 5324(a) (held) lists 'Executive Order Nos. 12138, 11246, 11701 and 11758'. The held eCFR texts of 31 CFR 202.4(e) and 31 CFR 203.6(e) cite 'Executive Order 11701' among the requirements applied to Federal contractors, and the Federal Register rule 75 FR 60249 (FR Doc. 2010-24218) lists 'Executive Order 11701, January 24, 1973 (3 CFR, 1971-1975 Comp., p. 752)' among the sources of the veterans employment rules. The later-events chain is empty and the OFR catalog search records no hit. Limit stated plainly: section 1 directs consultation with the Civil Service Commission, which the held evidence does not show how later law treated; the held evidence contains no instrument that ends section 1, so it is carried with the other continuing sections.

Presidential Documents
7259
Federal Register
Vol. 67, No. 33
Tuesday, February 19, 2002
Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 13257 of February 13, 2002
President’s Interagency Task Force To Monitor and Combat
Trafficking in Persons
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, including the Trafficking Victims
Protection Act of 2000, (22 U.S.C. 7103) (the ‘‘Act’’), and in order to combat
trafficking in persons, a contemporary manifestation of slavery whose victims
are predominantly women and children, to ensure just and effective punish-
ment of traffickers, and to protect their victims, it is hereby ordered as
follows:
Section 1. (a) The President’s Interagency Task Force to Monitor and Combat
Trafficking in Persons is hereby established.
(b) The Task Force shall consist of:
(i) the Secretary of State;
(ii) the Attorney General;
(iii) the Secretary of Labor;
(iv) the Secretary of Health and Human Services;
(v) the Director of Central Intelligence;
(vi) the Director of the Office of Management and Budget;
(vii) the Administrator of the United States Agency for International
Development; and
(viii) any additional officers or employees of the United States as may
be designated by the President.
(c) The Task Force shall be chaired by the Secretary of State.
Sec. 2. Activities. The Task Force shall, consistent with applicable law
and the constitutional authorities and duties of the President, carry out
the following activities:
(a) coordinate the implementation of the Act;
(b) measure and evaluate progress of the United States and other countries
in the areas of trafficking in persons prevention, protection, and assistance
to victims of trafficking in persons, and prosecutions and other enforcement
efforts against traffickers, including the role of public corruption in facili-
tating trafficking in persons;
(c) assist the Secretary of State in the preparation of the annual reports
described in section 110 of the Act;
(d) expand interagency procedures to collect and organize data, including
significant research and resource information on domestic and international
trafficking in persons, while ensuring that any data collection procedures
involved, respect the confidentiality of victims of trafficking in persons;
(e) engage in efforts to facilitate cooperation among countries of origin,
transit, and destination, and such efforts shall aim to strengthen local and
regional capacities to prevent trafficking in persons, prosecute traffickers
and assist trafficking victims; shall include initiatives to enhance cooperative
efforts between destination countries, transit countries, and countries of
origin; and shall assist in the appropriate reintegration of stateless victims
of trafficking in persons;

7260 Federal Register / Vol. 67, No. 33 / Tuesday, February 19, 2002 / Presidential Documents
(f) examine the role of the international ‘‘sex tourism ’’ industry in the
trafficking of persons and in the sexual exploitation of women and children
around the world;
(g) engage in consultation and advocacy with governmental and nongovern-
mental organizations, among other entities, to advance the purposes of the
Act; and
(h) address such other matters related to the purposes of the Act as
the President may determine.
Sec. 3. Administration. (a) The Department of State shall provide funding
and administrative support for the Task Force, except as otherwise provided
by the Act.
(b) At the call of the Chair, the Task Force shall meet as necessary
to accomplish its mission.
(c) Task Force members may designate representatives from their respective
agencies to represent them at Task Force meetings.
(d) Whenever the work of the Task Force involves a matter committed
by law or Presidential directive to the consideration of the National Security
Council, or by Executive Order 13228 of October 8, 2001, to the consideration
of the Homeland Security Council, that work shall be undertaken, and
any communication by the Secretary of State to the President shall be
undertaken, in a manner consistent with such law, Presidential directive,
or Executive Order.
(e) The Task Force shall have no directive authority or other substantial
independent authority.
(f) As necessary and appropriate, the Task Force shall report to the Presi-
dent, through the Secretary of State, the following:
(i) progress on the implementation of the Act; and
(ii) recommendations for United States policy to monitor and eliminate
trafficking in persons and to protect the victims of trafficking in persons.
Sec. 4. Judicial Review. This order does not create any rights or benefits,
enforceable at law or equity, against the United States, its departments,
its agencies, or other entities, its officers or employees, or any other person.
W

research_rationale:
EO 13257 (67 FR 7259, signed 2002-02-13; held official Federal Register text) establishes the President's Interagency Task Force to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons under the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000. The dossier inventory of 29 clauses was checked against the held original and covers sections 1 to 4: section 1 (establishment, membership list of eight named officers plus designees, and chair), section 2 (activities (a) to (h)), section 3 (administration (a) to (f)) and section 4 (judicial review); only the preamble recital is outside it. Two later orders amend the order and neither ends any clause. EO 13286 section 5 (68 FR 10619, signed 2003-02-28; held official text) inserts '(v) the Secretary of Homeland Security;' in section 1(b) and renumbers the later items; EO 13286 states 'This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003', so the amendment is recorded as effective 2003-03-01 (the order is published in the Federal Register of March 5, 2003). EO 13333 (69 FR 13455, signed 2004-03-18; held official text; it states no separate effective date, so the signing date is used) amends the preamble, redesignates section 4 as section 8 and adds new sections 4 to 7 (Senior Policy Operating Group guidelines and regulations, enhanced prevention, research, guidance for exercising authority), which are later additions and not original clauses. The dossier chain also lists an event attributed to EO 12977 (1995); that record is the dossier's note that EO 13286 section 23 amends EO 12977 and is not an amendment of EO 13257. Federal Register documents 2005-20549 and 2006-09855 and the CFR texts that cite the order recite it as a source of authority and do not amend or revoke it. The held U.S. Code note to 22 U.S.C. 7103 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 5, Feb. 28, 2003, 68 F.R. 10619; Ex. Ord. No. 13333, Mar. 18, 2004, 69 F.R. 13455' with no ending statement; the held current text of 22 U.S.C. 7103 still requires the President to establish an Interagency Task Force chaired by the Secretary of State and lists the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development among its members. The later-events chain and the OFR catalog hits for this order are the two amendments; no revocation or supersession appears. Limit stated plainly: the original list item naming the Director of Central Intelligence was not reconciled with later statutory changes to that office, because no held source states that this item ended; it is carried as written with the rest of section 1(b).

TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10110
P resid en t’s C o m m unications P olicy  
B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States, 
it is hereby ordered as follows :
1. There is hereby created a board to 
be known as the President’ s Communi­
cations Policy Board which shall be com­
posed of a chairman and four other 
members to be designated by the Presi­
dent.
2. It shall be the function of the Board 
to study the present and potential use 
of radio and wire communications facili­
ties by governmental and non-govern­
mental agencies and to make and present 
to the President evaluations and recom­
mendations in the national interest con­
cerning (a) policies for the most effective 
use of radio frequencies by governmental 
and non-governmental users and alter­
native administrative arrangements in 
the Federal Government for the sound 
effectuation of such policies, (b) policies 
with respect to international radio and 
wire communications, (c) the relation­
ship of Government communications to 
non-government communications, and 
(d) such related policy matters as the 
Board may determine.
3. The Board is authorized to hear and 
consult with representatives of industry 
and the Federal Government concerned 
with the subjects under study by the 
Board. All executive departments and 
agencies of the Federal Government are 
authorized and directed to cooperate with 
the Board in its work and to furnish the 
Board such information as it may re­
quire in the performance of its duties. 
The Board shall protect the security of 
any classified information submitted to 
it.
4. Each member of the Board shall, 
while away from his home or regular 
place of business and engaged in the 
official business of the Board, receive 
actual traveling expenses and per diem 
allowances in lieu of subsistence in ac­
cordance with rates established by the 
Standardized Government Travel Reg­
ulations, as amended.
5. During the fiscal year 1950 the ex­
penditures of the Board and the travel-
ing expenses and per diem allowances 
of the members thereof shall be paid out 
of an allotment made by the President 
from the appropriation appearing under 
the heading “Emergency Fund for the 
President” in the Independent Offices 
Appropriation Act, 1950 (Public Law 266, 
approved August 24, 1949); and during 
the fiscal year 1951 the same shall be 
similarly paid from any corresponding 
or like appropriation made available for 
the fiscal year 1951. Such payments 
shall be made without regard to the 
provisions of (a) section 3681 of the Re­
vised Statutes (31 U. S. C. 672), (b) sec­
tion 9 of the act of March 4, 1909, 35 
Stat. 1027 (31 U. S. C. 673), and (c) 
such other laws as the President may 
hereafter specify.
The Board shall terminate one year 
after the date of this order.
H arry  S. T ruman

February 17,1950.

research_rationale:
EO 10111 (15 FR 909, signed 1950-02-17; held official Federal Register text) approves a seal for the Central Intelligence Agency. It recites that section 2 of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 provides that the Director of Central Intelligence shall cause a seal of office to be made of a design the President approves, describes the seal's design in heraldic terms and makes the accompanying design part of the order, and states 'I hereby approve such seal as the official seal of the Central Intelligence Agency.' The dossier clause inventory (items 1-5, the President's Communications Policy Board) belongs to the adjacent Executive Order 10110 printed on the same Federal Register page; EO 10110's own text says 'The Board shall terminate one year after the date of this order', and that sentence is not part of EO 10111. The inventory is therefore replaced by two overrides cut from EO 10111's own text: the recitals and design description up to the page break (characters 3690-4439) and the continuation of the design description with the approval sentence (characters 11843-12508). EO 10111 has no term, condition or effective-date provision. The packet carries no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes it (later-events chain empty; the only actor record in the packet is EO 10110, an unrelated order about the President's Communications Policy Board printed on the same page), the bounded U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches record no hit naming the order, and nothing held ends the approval. Limit stated plainly: the current text of the authority statute (50 U.S.C. 3507, section 2 of the CIA Act of 1949) is not held in the repository, so the claim does not rest on it; the claim rests on the order's own text, which has no end, and on the absence of any later instrument in the bounded searches. The approval is a standing designation of the official seal; it was made on 1950-02-17 and nothing held shows it withdrawn or replaced.
